topic.title: Titan, June 2023: the sub's last routine message at 3,363 metres, then silence, then the hull gave way seven seconds later

title: Titan's Last Message Was Routine. Then the Sub Went Silent.
description:
The Titan submersible sent an ordinary message on its way down to the Titanic. Why did it never send another?
We rebuild Titan's last dive in 3D from the NTSB's final report: the routine message, the replies that got no answer, the water pressing on the carbon-fibre hull, and the moment it gave way.
The full minute-by-minute story is on the channel.
Sources: NTSB, ABC News (Oct 2025).
Based on official investigation reports and published sources. 3D scenes are reconstructions, not actual footage.
cta: The company or the rules: who should have stopped Titan? Comment

lines.text: Titan's last message was routine. Then it went silent.
It was 3,363 metres down, near the Titanic. So what happened?
On the ship, the crew typed a reply. Then another. No answer.
At the Titanic's depth, the sea presses 5,554.5 pounds on every square inch.
Holding it back: a carbon fibre tube, 5 inches thick.
But investigators found that wall was likely already damaged, its layers coming apart.
7 seconds after that message, the hull imploded. All 5 aboard died.
The company or the rules: who should have stopped Titan? Full story on our channel, from its last message.

Re-review of the changed loop line and cta ('The company or the rules: who should have stopped Titan?', on screen THE COMPANY / OR THE RULES?): blame stays within the reports. The NTSB MIR-25-36 probable cause is OceanGate's inadequate engineering process, and its contributing factors are insufficient voluntary guidance and US small passenger vessel regulations. The USCG report likewise faults OceanGate and calls for oversight and closing regulatory gaps. The line asks a question, names no individual and says no 'illegal'. The fail beat changed timing only, with no words or figures. Earlier fact confirmations stand and the disclaimer ends the description. Note: description says 'ABC News (Oct 2025)'; the article is Aug 2025.
